activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type II Regions

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/bc1b0ea463b0f753a2c65784fa5d46203cde8f457116c481301bf3f20ce82f54.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}4y\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/9bb9311cbaf796f76c4b8b7cb7ed81abec48abc445b894f838f940fbd92e534b.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 4-y-z},
$$

where

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/82f237dc5fb7d8b8ed34b7a1c16527ab338923a33462f0bd7dafbe54bc5e5158.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le 4-y-z}.
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}4y\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4-y-z}4y\,dx\,dz\,dy.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4-y-z}4y\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{4-y-z}4y\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}4y[x]_{x=0}^{x=4-y-z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}4y(4-y-z)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(16y-4{y}^{2}-4yz)\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(16y-4{y}^{2}-4yz)\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(16y-4{y}^{2}-4yz)\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[16yz-4{y}^{2}z-2y{z}^{2}]_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(14y-4{y}^{2})\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}(14y-4{y}^{2})\,dy & ={[7{y}^{2}-\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =(28-\frac{32}{3})-0 \\  & =\frac{52}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
